sentences.claim: MCDP 1 splits a mission into a task (what to do) and an intent (why), and states: "Of the two, the intent is predominant"
It says intent lets subordinates "depart from the original plan when the unforeseen occurs"
It describes a "top-down flow of intent" and expects subordinates to understand intent "at least two levels up"
Under mission tactics, "They inform the commander of what they have done, but they do not wait for permission"
The doctrine also names a single "main effort" that gets "priority for support of any kind," which means "exercising strict economy elsewhere"
The doctrine warns that decentralised initiative without some means of providing unity would "dissipate our strength"
Feynman wrote that "The acceptance and success of these flights is taken as evidence of safety," when in fact erosion was a warning "that something is wrong"
On schedule pressure, he wrote that "subtly, and often with apparently logical arguments, the criteria are altered so that flights may still be certified in time"
The Rogers Commission found "a relentless pressure on NASA to increase the flight rate"
It also found that NASA had required "a contractor to prove that it was not safe to launch, rather than proving it was safe"
The Columbia Board writes that "the higher information is transmitted in a hierarchy, the more it gets 'rolled-up,' abbreviated, and simplified"
It also warns that "The same conclusions, repeated over time, can result in problems eventually being deemed non-problems"
A key omission was "not technically a violation of NASA's own procedures," yet it showed "just how easily the flight preparation process can be compromised"
The wildfire guide says: "Accountability means to give an honest account"
It describes workers as "inheritors of the tools, trainings, procedures, the production incentives and the safety-vs.-production values of the workplace"
Its learning reviews assure participants "that there shall be no punitive actions"
sentences.missing: The assurance is limited to agency-imposed administrative punitive actions resulting from information gathered by the FLA team. It expressly does not protect against Department of Justice, Office of Inspector General or other outside authorities (source lines 1678–1687); the sentence omits this limitation.

sentences.claim: The guide also records that, after one fire, employees refused to talk to investigators because they did not expect fair treatment
The DOE handbook likewise endorses a culture where "people who make honest errors and mistakes are not blamed"
However, it calls such a committee "a temporary organization established in an advisory capacity" and says the need for one "is dependent upon the significance of the change"
It frames change management as error control: "Effective change management reduces the potential for error by managers when they modify their way of doing business"
It also argues that "most daily management activity involves some degree of change," such as changes to crew composition or schedules
The DOE handbook lists "Failure to establish performance indicators and track trends on the effectiveness of the corrective actions and lessons learned" as an at-risk practice
The marketing textbook prefers to "identify a handful of the most useful KPIs" over a "laundry list of 300 KPIs"
The DOE handbook ties safety to "the rigor with which people follow and perform work activities according to correctly written procedures, expectations, and standards"
The Columbia Board instead calls the ability to operate centrally or decentrally "when appropriate" "the hallmark of a high-reliability organization"
MCDP 1 says subordinates act without waiting for permission
Normal Accident Theory says failure-free aspirations are "inevitably doomed to fail"
The DOE handbook is more optimistic, describing HROs as "almost never experiencing an unwanted event"
After Challenger, the Rogers Commission recommended an independent safety office
The Columbia Board then found that "in-family," a category "introduced post-Challenger," meant "by definition the problems that were shifted into the lesser 'in-family' category got less attention"
The DOE model relies on a management champion with authority to devote resources
sentences.missing: The source presents one example change-management process, not a universal DOE model, and recommends identifying a champion, preferably someone with passion and authority to devote resources (lines 3085–3087 and 3100–3103). The categorical reliance on a resource-authorised champion overstates this qualified recommendation.

sentences.claim: The Scrum Guide gives the team itself the job of identifying improvements, saying "The most impactful improvements are addressed as soon as possible"
Meanwhile, the guide's equipment reviews lead directly to improvements and updated training
